items.title: Long-term memory for AI coding agents as a tree of plain files
items.summary_1line: Long-term memory for AI coding agents as a tree of plain files
items.editor_note: A file-tree implementation of long-term memory for coding agents.

editorial.tldr: A Sep 22 post asked how to evaluate agent memory beyond the context window. PACMI (Oct 5) then shifted the focus to keeping memory correct by invalidating stale entries.
editorial.whats_new: An open-source repo (Oct 11) stores coding-agent long-term memory as a tree of plain files, a simple alternative to a dedicated memory service.
editorial.why_it_matters: Agents that persist memory across sessions need an update and invalidation policy, not only a retrieval layer; plain-file stores make that state inspectable and diffable, but give you no invalidation for free.
editorial.take_for_builders: If your agent persists memory across sessions, record where each memory came from and test that correcting one fact also retires memories derived from it, whatever the storage backend.
